text:
nora: FYI found a crash in py-sdk when headers include both RateLimit-* and X-Client-Quota with different formats. stack trace points to json.loads on X-Client-Quota failing.

nora: example headers we logged:
RateLimit-Limit: 60
RateLimit-Remaining: "0"
Retry-After: 5
X-Client-Quota: {"pool":"svc-a","limit":50,"used":50}

ben: sounds familiar. we need a tolerant parser that normalizes numeric strings like "0" and meta formats like "60;w=60". also collapse duplicate RateLimit groups by taking the most restrictive (lowest remaining).

kai: async issue too: current approach has each task sleep on retry_after which causes thundering herd. propose central AsyncTokenBucket with Lock+Condition and monotonic refill. API idea: async with client.rate_limiter.guard(tokens=1).

nora: tests to add: header permutations, multi-header collapse, and concurrency stress where server returns Remaining=0 + Retry-After. expect no overshoot.

ben: typing: add normalize_rate_headers(...) -> TypedDict so callers get consistent ints/floats. log a single structured warning if parsing falls back.

ci-bot: created issue #3580: "py-sdk: tolerant header normalizer + central async rate limiter" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3580)

kai: i'll prototype the limiter and share perf numbers. will include jitter on wake to avoid sync.

nora: i'll open a small PR with normalizer and tests. thanks :)
